review_locator: PMCID:PMC3366176, Healing of intestinal inflammation by IL-22; PMID:32997932, The role of IL-22 in intestinal health and disease
primary_title: IL-22 ameliorates intestinal inflammation in a mouse model of ulcerative colitis; STAT3 links IL-22 signaling in intestinal epithelial cells to mucosal wound healing
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-22/STAT3 regulation of MUC1; the cited JCI and JEM primaries show STAT3-dependent mucus-associated MUC1 expression and epithelial function.
limitations_preserved: Distinguish MUC1 transcript from membrane mucin/protein and downstream barrier function; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3366176, Healing of intestinal inflammation by IL-22; PMCID:PMC8347589, Identification of an IL-22-Dependent Gene Signature as a Pharmacodynamic Biomarker
primary_title: DMBT1 is a novel gene induced by IL-22 in ulcerative colitis
decision_basis: The reviews identify DMBT1 as an IL-22-induced epithelial gene; the cited primary demonstrates IL-22/STAT3/NF-kappaB-dependent DMBT1 expression using transcript, promoter-deletion and EMSA assays.
limitations_preserved: Distinguish DMBT1 transcript from translated protein and any later epithelial or scavenger function; promoter and inhibitor evidence supports the IL-22 pathway in an epithelial/ulcerative-colitis context; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMID:32997932, The role of IL-22 in intestinal health and disease; PMCID:PMC4407497, Interleukin-22: immunobiology and pathology
primary_title: Innate lymphoid cell type 3-derived interleukin-22 boosts lipocalin-2 production in intestinal epithelial cells via synergy between STAT3 and NF-kappaB
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-22 regulation of epithelial LCN2; the cited primary shows IL-22-induced LCN2 transcript, IL-22 neutralization-sensitive ILC3-supernatant effects and STAT3/NF-kappaB cooperation, with LCN2 protein output under cytokine synergy.
limitations_preserved: IL-22 alone induces LCN2 transcript, while maximal protein output requires inflammatory cytokine synergy; distinguish LCN2 transcript from secreted protein and later enterobactin-binding biology; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

primary_title: Innate lymphoid cell type 3-derived interleukin-22 boosts lipocalin-2 production in intestinal epithelial cells via synergy between STAT3 and NF-kappaB
decision_basis: The reviews place IL-22 in the epithelial antimicrobial response; the cited primary reports a significant IL-22-associated increase in REG1A mRNA by qPCR in human intestinal epithelial cells.
limitations_preserved: Expression-level support only; no promoter/ChIP or REG1A protein assay is used here, so do not infer secretion or downstream antimicrobial function; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.
